title: Parker taken to hospital and the beach outings from Camarillo
summary: Parker was strapped down in the General Hospital and sent to Camarillo; friends took him out to play on the beach.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: And from then on, he went downhill, until they... One morning they called us up at Howard's house (I was living with Howard), and told us that they just had taken Charlie Parker to the County Hospital, that he had cracked up out there at the hotel. And so, Howard and I got up and we went out to the General Hospital to see him. They had him strapped down. But he never did lose his mental capacities. It was his nerves, see. And when we walked in, he spoke, and he told me, he says... He used to call me "Teddy Bear." He said, "Now, Teddy Bear, you go to the hotel and get my clothes and my horn," and he says, "And Howard is your witness." To let you know how he was thinking. He was all
strapped down! This is the way he was thinking, is that Howard McGhee is there; he'll be your witness. So his head was clear all the time, you see. And it wasn't...
How did he feel about being in the hospital?

Well, he knew that his body was wrecked, you know. His whole nervous system was gone. He had no control over his muscles or his nerves or anything. They just did anything they wanted to do. He couldn't direct their actions.

Anyway, a few days later, they put him in the Camarillo Hospital. And we used to go up to Camarillo a lot of times after we'd finished playing the after-hour places, especially Jack's Basket Room. Roy Porter and Sonny Criss and the guitar player, Chuck Norris, and Gene Montgomery, we'd take the horns and we'd take a snare drum and cymbals and everything, and the guitar, and take a horn for him, and we'd go to Camarillo, and they would let us take him out, and we would go down on to the beach and play -- so he could play some, you know. Go out on the beach.

But before that, when he was breaking down, I used to take him to the theatres. And that's the only way he seemed to rest, was that the music would put him to sleep. You know, while we were watching the movie, he'd listen to the music, and that's the only way he could rest a little bit.
Otherwise, he was just all shot. All of his his nerves were completely shot.
And we had many-many-many-many great moments up there, out there playing on the ocean...out on the beach, rather, and to get him out for a little while...

Oh yeah, he could play. He had all his facilities, once they got his nerves...once he got his energies back where his nerves were under control. And he was doing really good. And he always did talk, you know, with sense. He was never crazy really, you know.
